title.narrative: Boosting Productivity Through Human Capital Development Program (Subprogram 3)

description.narrative: This program provides a platform for the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to support the government to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth and to reduce poverty and inequality through the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The program (i) strengthens policies to finance and monitor the SDGs, (ii) improves educational attainment and skills development, and (iii) enhances social protection and public health systems. Subprogram 1 established the foundation of the program through regulatory reforms and pilot initiatives. Subprogram 2 concentrated on the implementation and expansion of reforms established under subprogram 1. Subprogram 3 focuses on institutionalizing those reforms, ensuring that they form a durable part of the national development framework.

Reform area: Strengthened Policies to Finance and Monitor Implementation of the SDGs
Outcome: Indonesia's Human Development Index improved to 0.760
Description: The government improved the quality and sustainability of health services by issuing regulations to (i) increase premium collections while incentivizing active participation from all non-subsidized beneficiaries, (ii) oblige regional governments to provide subsidies to poor and disadvantaged health insurance scheme participants; (iii) promote preventive health care through early screening of diseases, including cervical cancer, breast cancer, and anemia in adolescent girls, (iv) establish quality standards for gender-responsive inpatient treatment facilities, and (v) provide health insurance scheme members the right to choose their first level health facilities, empowering women to seek facilities where they feel safe and respected.

Action 1: The government issued regulations to expand coverage, improve benefits, and simplify benefit claims processes for formal sector workers enrolled in the unemployment benefit program.
Action 2: The government operationalized the unified beneficiary database to identify individuals and households eligible for social protection programs with: (i) clear procedures and mechanisms for verification, validation, and periodic data updates using information technology systems; (ii) enhanced data integration and accessibility across ministries and institutions; and (iii) strengthened data management capacity at the local level to reduce fragmentation of social protection schemes.
Action 3: The government, in line with the National Strategy on Stunting: (i) approved and implemented technical guidelines for simultaneous and coordinated public interventions to curb stunting nationwide, with specific targets relating to the wellbeing of pregnant women and children under 5; (ii) established a formal agreement with the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce to boost private sector efforts to prevent and reduce stunting; and (iii) approved guidelines for nutritional management in disaster and health crisis situations aimed at ensuring the resilience of crisis-affected communities, particularly women and other vulnerable groups
Action 4: The government continued implementing the Health Sector Transformation Agenda to support human capital development by: (i) approving policies aimed at improving health service delivery—including the implementation of reproductive health services and the establishment of minimum health service standards for essential care for pregnant women and mothers during childbirth—, amending the health sector's organizational structure, enhancing health system resilience, advancing health technology, and strengthening the health financing system; and (ii) increasing the health sector budget from Rp 76.56 trillion in 2023 to Rp 97.38 trillion in 2025 to support the transformation efforts.
